Subject: Kickoff: EU data-localization MAP & evaluation plan (multi-region)
Attachments: MAP_v0.1.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats), SOC2-evidence_inventory.pdf (application/pdf)

Hi Lena, Petr, and Nordica data team —

Thanks for agreeing to run a short mutual action plan (MAP) with us focused on EU data localization and cross-border review. The goal is to get to a clear evaluation decision and operational checklist within ~4 weeks so your procurement and legal teams can finalize the SOW and hosting locations.

High-level proposed timeline (suggested):
- Week 0 (this week): stakeholder alignment, roles, initial MAP spreadsheet populated (attached).
- Week 1: technical questionnaire and flow diagram review; onboarding of DPO & infra reviewers.
- Week 2: evidence collection (SOC2 artifacts, controls mapping).
- Week 3: finalize controls, confirm hosting region and transfer mechanisms (SCCs / EDPS guidance), sign-off.

Key asks from you to start:
1) Please confirm the primary DPO / contact for legal & data protection (name + email).
2) Confirm any pre-existing vendor restrictions (e.g., absolute EU-only residency, approved third-party processors).
3) Availability for a 45-minute kickoff call on Thursday, 21 May at 11:00 CEST (we can shift if needed).

I've attached the initial MAP workbook (MAP_v0.1.xlsx) with proposed owners and a placeholder evidence inventory (SOC2-evidence_inventory.pdf). Marissa (CS) and Neha (Solutions) are looped on the MAP and will drive technical and evidence collection, respectively. Stephanie (Legal) will support contract-level questions and any requested SCC language.

If helpful, we can add a column for 'must-stay-in-EU' boolean flags and a separate tab for third-party processors.

Next steps from our side: I will book the kickoff call once I have confirmation of DPO and a preferred time. Please reply with the point people and any immediate constraints.

Best,

Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

Hi Vanessa —

Thanks, this looks good and aligned to what Legal wants to see. Our DPO is Claudia Weber (cc'd) — she will own the privacy review and will work with Infra on the dataflow diagram (attached). A few quick constraints from our side:
- We require EU residency for all customer data at rest unless an explicit transfer justification is provided and SCCs are in place.
- Any subprocessors outside the EEA need a pre-approval step; Tomas Alvarez at CloudProc (copied on separate thread) will be the infra contact for third-party processing.

Kickoff time: 21 May at 11:00 CEST works for Claudia and me. Please send a calendar invite and we will have Legal + Infra on the call.

Thanks Lena — great, and welcome Claudia. I populated the MAP_v0.1.xlsx with an initial set of owners and dates (see tab "Owners & Milestones"). Quick owner callouts:
- Claudia (DPO): privacy review, legal sign-off — target May 27
- Petr (Infra/Tech): architecture & dataflow confirmation — target May 25
- Marissa (CS): evidence coordination with your customer success — ongoing
- Neha (Solutions): SOC2 artifacts + controls mapping — target June 2

Action items before the kickoff call:
- Claudia / Legal: confirm which controls we should prioritize in the evidence inventory (privacy-by-design, data-at-rest encryption, key management).
- Petr / Infra: confirm whether any in-scope subprocessors are US-based and list them in the MAP.
- Nordica procurement: share any mandatory contractual terms or timeline constraints (e.g., procurement committee on June 10).

I'll bring a short evaluation plan to the kickoff that maps each MAP milestone to a pass/fail criteria and the minimal evidence we need. We will use the HubSpot deal page and the Drive MAP folder for all artifacts.

On a practical note: I will create a Slack channel #rdw-nordica-dataprotection if Nordica is comfortable (invites to the infra contact). It typically helps speed evidence collection.

Thanks — looking forward.
